# Reference


Quick reference: a command cheat sheet, a symptom-to-fix troubleshooting index, and a glossary.


## Cheat sheet {#sec-cheatsheet}

Everything you'll reach for, on one page.

### Connect

```bash
ssh <username>@medicinebow.arcc.uwyo.edu     # after SSH Key Manager setup
# Portal: https://medicinebow.arcc.uwyo.edu   (Open OnDemand)
# Keys expire yearly → regenerate in the portal's SSH Key Manager
```

### Storage (nothing is backed up)

```bash
arccquota                  # usage vs. limits for home / scratch / project
du -sh * | sort -h         # what's eating my quota here?
```

| Path | Quota | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `/home/$USER` | 50 GB | small; config only |
| `/project/cowy-firesurro` | 5 TB | shared group data |
| `/gscratch/$USER` (`$SCRATCH`) | 5 TB | fast, purged after 90 days idle |
| `/project/<proj>/software` | +250 GB | put conda/containers here |
| `/lscratch` | node-local | **wiped at job end** |

### Modules

```bash
module spider <name>       # does it exist? what to load first? (use THIS, not avail)
module load gcc/14.2.0 <pkg>
module purge               # clean slate
module save <name> / module restore <name>
```

### Submit and manage jobs

```bash
sbatch submit.sh           # submit batch job
salloc -A cowy-firesurro --qos=interactive -t 2:00:00 -c 4 --mem=16G   # interactive
squeue --me                # my jobs
showjobreasons <id>        # why is it waiting? (plain English)
scancel <id>               # cancel (scancel --me = all mine)
seff <id>                  # after the fact: was it sized right?
sacct -j <id> --format=JobID,State,Elapsed,MaxRSS,ReqMem,ExitCode
```

### Minimal submit script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=cowy-firesurro     # REQUIRED — project, not username
#SBATCH --job-name=myjob
#SBATCH --partition=mb               # default CPU pool
#SBATCH --qos=fast                   # 12h, high priority
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=16G                    # ALWAYS set memory (mb default is 10G/core!)
#SBATCH --output=slurm-%j.out

module purge
module load gcc/14.2.0 python/3.12.0
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK
python my_script.py
```

### Choosing partition + QOS

| Goal | `--partition` | `--qos` |
|---|---|---|
| "Does it run?" (tiny test) | `debug` | `debug` (1 h, instant) |
| Fast CPU test (≤12 h) | `mb` | `fast` |
| Interactive dev | `mb` | `interactive` |
| Normal CPU job (<3 d) | `mb` or `mb,teton` | `normal` |
| Long CPU sim (3–7 d) | `non-investor` | `long` |
| GPU dev / proof-of-concept | `mb-a30` | `normal` |
| GPU production run | `mb-h100` / `mb-l40s` | `normal`/`long` |

**QOS ceilings & priority:** `interactive` 8h/p90 · `fast` 12h/p80 · `normal` 3d/p70 ·
`long` 7d/p60 · `debug` 1h/p0. **Priority is dominated by QOS** (weight 200 vs age 10) —
pick the shortest tier your job fits.

### GPUs

```bash
#SBATCH --partition=mb-l40s
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1                 # or gpu:h100:2 for a specific type/count
module load gcc/13.2.0 cuda-toolkit/12.6.1   # CUDA needs gcc 13.2 (deprecated but required)
gpuavail                             # free GPUs by type, right now
nvidia-smi / nvtop                   # is my code actually using the GPU?
```

### Job arrays

```bash
#SBATCH --array=1-500%20             # 500 tasks, ≤20 at once (max array size 10000)
#SBATCH --output=logs/%A_%a.out
python run.py --id ${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}
```

### Check the live queue before a big submit

```bash
showpartitions             # idle vs busy nodes per partition
gpuavail                   # free GPUs now
sinfo -p mb-h100 -o "%P %t %D"
showuserlimits             # what am I allowed to ask for?
```

### Common mistakes to avoid

- `--account=<project>` is **required** on every job.
- On `mb`, no `--mem` → **10 GB per core** silently. Always set `--mem`.
- **Nothing is backed up.** Keep a copy off-cluster.
- Install software in `/project/<proj>/software`, not `/home` (50 GB).
- `module spider`, not `module avail`.
- Long jobs → `non-investor` partition **and** checkpoint (investors preempt).
- Never compute on the login node. Use `sbatch`/`salloc`.
- Use `tmux` so a dropped connection doesn't kill interactive work.


## Troubleshooting {#sec-troubleshooting}

A symptom-first index to the rest of the book.

### Login and access

**"Permission denied (publickey)" when I `ssh` — it worked before.**
Your SSH key almost certainly **expired** (they last one year). Regenerate it in the portal's
SSH Key Manager, unzip into `~/.ssh`, `chmod 0600 -R ~/.ssh` (@sec-first-login).

**"Permission denied" on a brand-new setup.**
Check permissions: `chmod 0600 -R ~/.ssh`, and make sure you unzipped the key into `~/.ssh`.
Confirm you're using `medicinebow.arcc.uwyo.edu`, not the dead `southpass` name.

**I can't get an account at all.**
Only a **PI** can request it, in writing, against a project. You cannot self-register
(@sec-account).

**Globus won't let me add the collection.**
If you're an external collaborator on an **ARCC-Only account**, you can't use Globus. You need
a UW-side guest collection (@sec-moving-data).

### Jobs won't submit

**`sbatch: error: ... You have to specify an account.`**
Add `--account=cowy-firesurro` (@sec-anatomy).

**`Job violates accounting/QOS policy (...)` at submit time.**
Your request exceeds a QOS limit (every QOS is `DenyOnLimit`). Usually `--time` exceeds the
QOS ceiling — e.g. 5 days under `normal` (max 3 d). Lower `--time` or switch QOS
(@sec-partitions). Check ceilings with `sqos` and `showuserlimits`.

**`Invalid qos specification`.**
Your account can't use that QOS. Yours are `debug, fast, interactive, long, normal`
(`sacctmgr -n show assoc user=$USER format=qos`).

### Jobs won't start

**Stuck in `PENDING` with reason `Priority`.**
The machine is just busy and you're in line. Either wait, or pick a higher-priority (shorter)
QOS — QOS dominates priority here (@sec-priority). Small/short jobs backfill sooner.

**Stuck with reason `Resources`.**
You asked for a lot (many cores, much memory, a scarce GPU). Right-size (@sec-resources), or
accept the wait. `showjobreasons <id>` explains in plain language.

**GPU job pending for hours.**
H100/L40S are heavily contended (@sec-queue-times). Develop on `mb-a30` instead, and check
`gpuavail`/`showpartitions` for what's actually free before submitting.

**Pending with `QOSMax...` or `AssocGrpCpuLimit`.**
You (or your account) hit a cap — e.g. too many cores in flight at once. Wait for your other
jobs to finish, or throttle an array with `%` (@sec-arrays).

### Jobs fail

**`OUT_OF_MEMORY`.**
Raise `--mem`. Compare `MaxRSS` to `ReqMem` in `sacct` (@sec-fail). Watch the 10 GB/core
default trap (@sec-resources).

**`TIMEOUT`.**
Job outran `--time`. Checkpoint (@sec-checkpointing), raise `--time` within the QOS ceiling,
or split the work into an array.

**`FAILED`, worked interactively but not in batch.**
You loaded modules / activated conda on the login node but not **inside the submit script**.
Put them in the script (@sec-anatomy, @sec-conda).

**Output file references files that "don't exist."**
Relative paths from the wrong directory, or you wrote to `/lscratch` (wiped at job end). Use
absolute paths or `$SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR`; copy `/lscratch` output out before the job ends
(@sec-storage).

**`PREEMPTED` / `REQUEUED` on a long job.**
You were on investor hardware and got reclaimed. Move to `--partition=non-investor` and
checkpoint (@sec-preemption).

### Software

**"That module doesn't exist" but I'm sure it does.**
`module avail` only shows what's reachable now. Use `module spider <name>` — you probably need
to load a compiler first (@sec-modules).

**CUDA won't build / link.**
Load `gcc/13.2.0` (not 14) — `cuda-toolkit` is built against 13.2 despite its deprecation
warning (@sec-modules).

**Home directory full, everything breaking.**
Conda in `/home`. Move envs to `/project/<proj>/software` via `~/.condarc`, and clean up
(@sec-conda). Check with `du -sh ~/* | sort -h`.

**GPU job runs but is slow / `nvidia-smi` shows 0%.**
Your code isn't actually on the GPU. Verify the framework sees CUDA; in a container, you need
`--nv` (@sec-gpu).

### Still stuck?

Email **`arcc-help@uwyo.edu`** with your **job ID**, the submit script, and the error. Or
bring it to **office hours, Tuesdays 11am–1pm** on Zoom. Include what you already tried — it
gets you a faster answer.


## Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Plain-language definitions of the terms this book uses.

**Account (Slurm)**
: The *project* that a job is charged to (e.g. `cowy-firesurro`). Required on every job via
  `--account`. Not your username. See @sec-anatomy.

**ARCC**
: Advanced Research Computing Center — the UW group that runs MedicineBow.

**ASCEND / ARID**
: The NSF Regional Innovation Engine (ASCEND) and its wildfire-resilience program (ARID) that
  many readers of this book work under. See the preface.

**Backfill**
: Slurm slotting a small, short job into a gap in the schedule without delaying higher-priority
  jobs. Why short jobs start fast. See @sec-priority.

**Batch job**
: A job submitted as a script with `sbatch` that runs unattended when scheduled. The normal way
  to run work. See @sec-anatomy.

**Checkpoint**
: A periodic save of a job's state so it can *resume* instead of *restart* after a preemption,
  timeout, or crash. Essential for long jobs. See @sec-checkpointing.

**Compute node**
: A machine where computation actually runs, allocated to you by Slurm. Distinct from a login
  node. See @sec-cluster.

**Condo model**
: The funding model where research groups buy nodes (`inv-*`) and others borrow them when idle,
  subject to reclaim/preemption. See @sec-preemption.

**Core-hour**
: One CPU core used for one hour — the unit your allocation is measured in. Reserving 8 cores
  for 1 hour costs 8 core-hours whether or not you use them.

**`DenyOnLimit`**
: A QOS flag meaning an over-limit request is **rejected at submit time**, not silently queued.
  See @sec-partitions.

**Fair-share**
: A priority factor reflecting your account's recent usage relative to its share; heavy recent
  use temporarily lowers your priority. See @sec-priority.

**GRES (Generic RESource)**
: How you request GPUs: `--gres=gpu:1` or `--gres=gpu:h100:2`. See @sec-gpu.

**Investor / `inv-*`**
: Nodes/partitions owned by a specific group, who get top priority; others can be preempted off
  them. See @sec-preemption.

**Job array**
: One script run many times with a varying index (`$SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID`), for parameter sweeps
  and ensembles. Max 10,000 tasks. See @sec-arrays.

**Lmod / module**
: The system that loads specific software versions into your shell on demand. Hierarchical:
  many modules are hidden until you load a compiler. Use `module spider`. See @sec-modules.

**Login node**
: The shared front-end machine (`mblog1`, `mblog2`) you land on when you connect. For editing
  and submitting — **not** for computing. See @sec-cluster.

**MedicineBow**
: UW/ARCC's current flagship HPC cluster. The subject of this book.

**MPI**
: Message Passing Interface — the standard for a single parallel program spanning many cores or
  nodes that communicate. Launched with `srun`. Contrast with job arrays. See @sec-ladder.

**OnDemand (Open OnDemand)**
: The web portal at `medicinebow.arcc.uwyo.edu` — file browser, terminal, and interactive apps.
  See @sec-first-login.

**OOM (Out Of Memory)**
: When a job exceeds its memory reservation and is killed. Fix by raising `--mem`. See @sec-fail.

**Partition**
: A named pool of nodes with particular hardware (`mb`, `mb-h100`, `teton`, `non-investor`, …).
  Chosen with `--partition`. See @sec-partitions.

**Preemption**
: An investor reclaiming a borrowed node, causing your job to be killed and (here) requeued.
  See @sec-preemption.

**Priority**
: The score that orders pending jobs. On MedicineBow it's dominated by QOS (weight 200). See
  @sec-priority.

**QOS (Quality of Service)**
: The service tier that sets your max walltime, resource cap, and priority (`debug`, `fast`,
  `normal`, `long`, …). See @sec-partitions.

**Requeue**
: Putting a killed (preempted/failed) job back in the pending queue to start over. Pair with
  checkpointing. See @sec-preemption.

**Scratch (`/gscratch`, `$SCRATCH`)**
: Fast, large, temporary storage purged after 90 days of inactivity. Not backed up. See
  @sec-storage.

**`seff`**
: A command showing a finished job's CPU and memory efficiency — use it to right-size. See
  @sec-monitoring.

**Slurm**
: The scheduler that manages all jobs on the cluster. See @sec-why-scheduler.

**Snapshot**
: A point-in-time copy of a filesystem, on the *same array* as the live data. Protects against
  accidental deletion, **not** hardware loss. Not a backup. See @sec-storage.

**Walltime**
: Real elapsed clock time a job is allowed (`--time`). The job is killed at the limit. See
  @sec-resources.
